statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail falls from 24 to 17, back into the low band, because the single decisive piece of evidence the previous assessment could not score has now resolved. NQ futures were verified at 29,161.00, down 287.75 points or 0.98%, roughly 117 points above a 29,044.25 session low that held rather than extending. Cash NAS100 at 29,161.85 trades near its 29,177.14 session high after opening the auction at its 29,038.22 low, so the opening auction reversed rather than continued. Brent has eased to 104.05, up 2.80%, from 105.30 and up 4.04% earlier, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.91% and the 2-year 4.53%, both marginally off their highs, and E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,594.75 sit near their own session low, which is dispersion rather than a uniform one-way tape. VIX at 17.98, up 9.25%, is the one conflicting signal. A meaningful retracement, a session low that held through the first full cash hour and cross-assets easing off their extremes remove the amplifier stack that lifted tail to the top of the watch band.
recommendation: Tail at 17 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The previous danger window over the cash open has expired and its central condition, opening-auction continuation, was not observed. The narrow evidence-based danger window therefore moves forward to 12:30-13:30 UTC on 11 September, covering the August consumer price index and the first hour of post-release price discovery, which is the next scheduled point at which a no-retracement structure could form. Conditional tail peaks at 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot tomorrow and 21 in the hour after, the only two slots in the window mapped to the watch band. Within today's session the conditional path holds between 15 and 18, with the local high at 18 in the 19:00 UTC power hour where closing-auction flow can extend a day that is still net lower. Stress remains extreme at 84 because the energy-led inflation impulse, an ECB that raised rates today with effect from 16 September and a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September are all unresolved. Stress at that level describes the environment and does not on its own move the mapped state past the block threshold.
headline: NQ retraces about 117 points off a 29,044.25 low that held, and cash NAS100 trades near its session high after opening at its low; tail eases from 24 to 17
body:
The conditional peak that the previous assessment placed in this hour has been tested and not confirmed. That assessment set tail at 24, the top of the watch band, expressly because NQ had extended to a new 29,043.25 session low after the producer price release and was sitting about twenty points above it, with the decisive question, whether the opening auction would continue the trend, roughly one minute old and unscoreable. It is now scoreable, and the answer is that the trend did not continue.

NQ futures were verified at 29,161.00, down 287.75 points or 0.98% from a 29,448.75 close, against a session range of 29,044.25 to 29,508.25. The low is essentially unchanged from the 29,043.25 observed an hour ago, meaning it was not extended, and price has recovered roughly 117 points from it. The cash index confirms this independently: the Nasdaq-100 stands at 29,161.85 against a session range of 29,038.22 to 29,177.14, which places it within about fifteen points of its session high after having opened at its session low. Two separate series, the continuous futures contract and the cash index, agree both on the level and on the shape. For a mean-reversion book the relevant fact is not that the index is lower on the day but that a retracement of real size occurred and the prior low was respected.

The cross-asset stack that supported the elevated reading has also loosened at the margin rather than tightened. Brent crude trades at 104.05, up 2.80% on the day, against 105.30 and up 4.04% an hour ago; the energy-led inflation impulse is still the dominant macro story of the week, driven by the seventh month of U.S.-Iran conflict and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, but oil is no longer pressing its highs. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.91% and the 2-year 4.53%, against 4.92% and 4.52% previously, so the long end has stopped extending even though it remains at a multi-year high, and the 30-year is 5.33%. The one genuine conflict is VIX at 17.98, up 9.25% and near its 18.05 session high, which is a higher print than the 17.61 observed an hour ago. An absolute level near 18 does not describe a disorderly market, but the direction is the one piece of evidence pointing the other way and it is the main reason tail eases to 17 rather than lower.

Dispersion remains wide and remains informative. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,594.75 are down 0.64% and sit close to their 7,585.50 session low, so the broad index has not participated in the Nasdaq contract's recovery. That divergence is consistent with a duration-sensitive de-rating that is now being partially unwound in the growth complex, rather than with a broad risk-off cascade. A uniform one-way tape across both contracts would have been a genuine amplifier; two contracts moving differently is close to the opposite.

The releases behind the move are unchanged and were not the hawkish shock that pre-market positioning appeared to anticipate. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the producer price index for final demand rose 0.4% in August and 5.4% over twelve months, with the measure excluding foods, energy and trade services up 0.3% on the month and 4.7% on the year; the headline matched consensus and the core measures came in at or below it. The European Central Bank raised its three key rates by 25 basis points this morning, taking the deposit facility to 2.50% with effect from 16 September, citing Middle East conflict as a continuing source of inflation pressure.

Stress stays at 84, deep in the extreme band, and that is deliberate. Nothing structural has resolved: oil above 104, a ten-year yield at 4.91%, a European central bank that tightened today and a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September all remain live, and the August consumer price index lands inside the final slots of the forward window. High stress coexisting with low tail is the accurate description of this environment, and stress on its own does not move the mapped state.

The forward path reflects the resolution rather than the fear. Conditional tail holds between 15 and 18 across the U.S. session, with a local high of 18 in the 19:00 UTC power hour where closing-auction flow can extend a day that is still net lower. It falls to a 10 floor across the Asian session, then climbs one to two points per hour through the European morning to 18 in the hour before the consumer price index, 23 in the slot containing the 12:30 UTC release and 21 in the hour after. Only those last two slots map to the watch band. That anticipatory climb is expressed mainly through rising stress and falling confidence, from 88 to 69 across the window, because a scheduled release is a checkpoint and not an observed price path, and today's sequence is a useful reminder that a hawkish-looking setup can produce extension followed by orderly retracement rather than a lethal trend.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 14:00 UTC on 9 September to 13:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 10 in the 14:00 UTC slot on 9 September, ticks to 16 in the following hour on an event/whipsaw read, then settles into a 13 to 8 band across the U.S. close and the overnight session, with the low print of 8 in the 00:00 UTC hour. The Asian and early European hours of 10 September held a narrow 9 to 11 range with a mixed dominant mode and confidence steady at 87 to 88. The final three slots carry the turn: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode switched to trend-down and the pre-release grind became directional, tail 20 at 12:00 UTC with the mapped state at WATCH around the producer price release, and tail 24 at 13:00 UTC read as trend-down after the release extended the session low. Stress never left the extreme band across the whole window, ranging from 80 to 86, which is the clearest signal that a difficult high-volatility environment coexisted with a tail score that stayed below the block threshold for all 24 hours. Past assessments are reported exactly as published and are not revised using later information.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with the previous assessment's conditional peak resolved against continuation and closes on a consumer price release. Conditional tail starts at 17 in the current 14:00 UTC hour, eases to 16 and then 15 through the middle of the cash session, ticks to 16 at 18:00 UTC and reaches a U.S.-session high of 18 in the 19:00 UTC power hour, where closing-auction flow can extend a day that is still net lower. It then decays through 16 and 13 into the close, reaching 11 and 10 by late evening and holding a 10 floor across the Asian session. From the European pre-open it climbs gradually through 11, 12, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16 to 18 in the hour before the August consumer price index, then 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot that contains the 12:30 UTC release and 21 in the hour after it. Those final two slots are the only ones in the window mapped to the watch band, and the danger window is drawn narrowly around them at 12:30 to 13:30 UTC on 11 September. The anticipatory climb deliberately raises stress and lowers confidence more than it raises tail, because hypothetical post-event alignment is not treated as observed structure. Stress runs from 84 down to a 76 overnight trough and back to 86 in the release slot, never leaving the extreme band. Confidence falls from 88 to 69 across the window, reflecting how much of the forward path depends on price structure that has not yet formed. Beyond the window, the Federal Reserve decision, projections and press conference on 16 September remain the dominant scheduled risk.
